recentItems.title: Bronx News Today: Multiple shootings, subway stabbing and missing teen cases under investigation
recentItems.description:
Several investigations are underway across the Bronx after a 23-year-old woman was shot on Adee Avenue, a 45-year-old man was shot near St. Mary’s Park Houses in Melrose, and a 49-year-old man was shot in the Concourse section. Police are also searching for the suspect who stabbed a 46-year-old man at the Fordham Road B and D subway station. Elsewhere, two workers suffered non-life-threatening injuries after a partial construction collapse in Mott Haven, while police continue searching for missing teen Thompson, last seen leaving his Baychester Avenue home on June 13. Community leaders also launched the Bronx Says No to Hunger initiative to address food insecurity.

recentItems.title: "9/11 didn't end on 9/11": Civilian cancers now outpace first responders
recentItems.description:
It's been 25 years since 9/11 - but the health crisis left behind is far from over. Federal data shows the number of people with 9/11-linked cancers is still growing - especially among civilians. Michael Barasch, who represents more than 50,000 people in the 9/11 community, says  civilian cancer cases have surpassed those of first responders for the first time. That increase is staggering: more than 3,200% in a decade.
Nearly 3,000 people died on Sept. 11, and at least 9,400 more people have since died from 9/11-related illnesses - more than triple the original death toll.

More on News12.com: https://brooklyn.news12.com/911-didnt-end-on-911-civilian-cancers-now-outpace-first-responders

recentItems.title: Drone helps save swimmer swept away by current on Long Island
recentItems.description:

Southampton officials say the area is known for strong currents and urge swimmers to choose lifeguarded beaches whenever possible.

recentItems.title: 3 officers and captain injured in Rikers Island attack
recentItems.description:
Four correction staff members, including a captain, were injured during an incident Saturday afternoon at the Otis Bantum Correctional Center on Rikers Island. Police said a person attacked three uniformed officers and a captain, though authorities could not immediately say exactly what happened. The incident comes as New York City continues efforts to close Rikers Island and transition to borough-based prisons, a plan that is facing delays.
